أَلَصُّ , (S, M, K,) or أَلَصُّ الأَضْرَاسِ, (A,) A man (M, A) whose [teeth called] اضراس are near together (S, M, A, K) so that no interstice is seen between them: (M:) as also أَرَصُّ: (M, A, K, art. رص:) fem. لَصَّآءُ. (M.) ―
-b2- Also, the masc. (As, TA) and fem., (K,) or أَلَصُّ الفَخِذَيْنِ, (A,) One whose thighs cleave together, there being no space between them. (As, A, * K.) [See also أَرَصُّ.] Hence, (TA,) the Zenjee is said to be أَلَصُّ الأَلْيَتَيْنِ, (K,) i. e. Having the buttocks cleaving together. (TA.) And أَلَصُّ, (S,) or أَلَصُّ المَنْكِبَيْنِ, (A,) Having the two shoulderjoints near together, almost touching the ears. (S, A.) ―
-b3- Also the fem., applied to a woman, Impervia coëunti; (M;) as also رَصَّآءُ. (M, art. رص.) ―
-b4- And, applied to a forehead (جَبْهَة), Narrow. (K.) ―
-b5- And, applied to a sheep or goat, Having one of her horns extending forwards and the other backwards. (Z, Sgh, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
